pl900824968.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl900824968.description: A Bronze Age archaeological site with Deer Stones located at Uushigiin Ovor (UO), Mongolia, that is included in the cultural landscape "Deer Stone Monuments and Related Bronze Age Sites", inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023.

pl159950110.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl159950110.description: Ritual complex in central Mongolia consisting of eight deer stone monuments surrounded by nine stone rings and several cairns.

pl707475714.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl707475714.description: Burial site in western Mongolia containing a stone cairn and several deer stone monuments, dated to the 8th-7th centuries BCE.

pl537384980.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl537384980.description: Burial site in Zavkhan Province, Mongolia containing over 150 burials dated to the Xiongnu period.

cur-fossil-shishugou.dateNote: In 1987 the Sino-Canadian Dinosaur Project found a big meat-eater in these rocks of the Junggar Basin, Xinjiang, named Sinraptor in 1994. Later digs found Guanlong, an early tyrannosaur. The rock is about 160 million years old (Late Jurassic). Wikidata pins the formation at a rounded point.
cur-fossil-shishugou.summary: Late Jurassic rocks in Xinjiang that gave Sinraptor and the early tyrannosaur Guanlong.
